subject: Systems integrator onramp: scoping + data path options (EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Elena Popov <elena.popov@edgeworks.co>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:17:00 +0100
Subject: Systems integrator onramp: scoping + data path questions

Hi Monica / Vivek,

Thanks again for the intro call this week — NorthPoint is excited to explore an alliance. Before we draft an MOU, a few practical questions from our engineering and privacy teams so we can scope the POC and estimate delivery:  

- Data residency: can Redwood guarantee that inference requests and KV cache materialize only in a customer-controlled EU region for an EU-located tenant? If the SI runs a managed connector, what telemetry is shared?
- Enclave options: do you offer a managed VPC connector or a deployable on-prem enclave package for private deployments? We need details on network egress and whether HSM-backed keys are supported.
- Audit logs / evidence: we'd like a checklist of what logs (token-level, request/response, model version) are retained and for how long by default.
- POC scope and resourcing: proposed 2-week technical onramp (connectivity + sample workload) — can you provide a rough SOW (hours + roles)?

Attaching a short list of our compliance questions (attached: NP_Prelim_Questions.pdf) and a skeleton timeline. Can Vivek and Monica confirm who on Redwood will be our technical lead and security contact?

Best,
Elena
Partnerships Director
EdgeWorks / NorthPoint collaboration team

Attachment: NP_Prelim_Questions.pdf (questions list)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Popov <elena.popov@edgeworks.co>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Systems integrator onramp: scoping + data path questions

Elena — thanks, this is great detail and very actionable. Short answers up front, then a proposal for next steps:  

- Residency: yes — for Redwood Private we can pin compute to a customer EU region and disable cross-region routing. For Hosted flows we offer region-scoped routing policies and a data residency SLA for enterprise plans.
- Enclave: we have a VPC connector (managed) and an on-prem package (installer + thin control plane) that supports KMS/HSM. We'll share the deployment matrix.
- Audit logs: default retention is 90 days for request/response traces; token-level telemetry can be exported to the customer's SIEM via our event stream. We will provide an evidence pack for SOC2 items during the POC.
- POC SOW: typical onramp is 10-15 engineer-days (integration, test prompts, runbook + handoff). I attached our "SI_Onramp_Checklist.xlsx" and a lightweight sketch of the expected data path.

Proposed next steps:
1) 2-week technical POC focused on one EU customer: connectivity + sample workload + residency verification.
2) Parallel security questionnaire exchange (we will provide evidence artifacts).
3) Draft MOU to cover responsibilities and liability during the POC (Hiro will take lead for the MOU).

Can you confirm the customer and the EU region you prefer (e.g., Frankfurt, Paris)? Once you confirm I'll schedule a kickoff and loop in Marissa for enablement materials.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0123

Attachments: SI_Onramp_Checklist.xlsx, DataFlowSketch.png

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Systems integrator onramp: scoping + data path questions

Looping in a couple quick technical clarifications so our POC SOW is accurate:  

- KV / cache behavior: during a pinned Private deployment the KV cache stays in-region. For Hosted we can enable prefix-aware caching with customer-controlled TTLs; we'll provide a config template.
- Network and egress: the managed VPC connector initiates egress only to configured IP ranges. For an on-prem enclave we recommend a NAT-proxied control channel with outbound-only connectivity for updates.
- Token telemetry: we must be careful about what we classify as PII. We can deliver anonymized token logs to the SIEM and full request traces under NDA.

Action items for the POC SOW:
- Define a staging subnet and a test dataset (redacted) for residency verification.
- 8h of Redwood infra eng time for connector install + 12h for integration/testing.
- 4h for security artifact handoff (evidence pack).

Hiro — can you draft a minimal MOU covering liabilities during the POC and the data flows? I'll include these time estimates in the HubSpot deal.

-Vivek
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Popov <elena.popov@edgeworks.co>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Systems integrator onramp: scoping + data path questions — MOU and timelines

Elena / team — thanks for the patience. Draft MOU attached (MOU_NorthPoint_draft.pdf) and a short timeline below. This MOU is intentionally narrow — it covers the 2-week technical POC only and sets clear boundaries on data handling, audit evidence, and liability during testing. Key points:  

- Scope: connectivity, residency verification, evidence handoff. No production inference traffic or customer data besides redacted test corpus.
- Roles: Redwood provides connector, infra engineering hours, and audit pack; NorthPoint/EdgeWorks provides staging subnet and partner engineer for integration and acceptance testing.
- Security controls: HSM-backed keys supported for on-prem package; event stream export under NDA; logs retained 90 days unless otherwise negotiated.
- Escalation: severity process and contact list included; automatic rollback clause if cross-region routing is observed.

Next steps:
1) Elena — please review MOU and confirm by EOD Thursday 12 Nov. Sign via DocuSign link below when ready.
2) Monica/Marissa/Vivek — I'll convert the MOU to a short Statement of Work and attach to the HubSpot deal ND-5843.
